name: Simic Sky Swallower
oracle_text:
Flying, trample
Shroud (This creature can't be the target of spells or abilities.)
blocked_sentences: Shroud (This creature can't be the target of spells or abilities.)

needs.what: a `shroud` member on `Keyword` (src/automtg/engine/enums.py) plus a check in `can_be_targeted` (src/automtg/engine/targeting.py) that refuses the object to *every* controller, evaluated before the `obj.controller == controller` early return that currently short-circuits hexproof. It is the target rule only: shroud does not touch damage, blocking or enchant/equip, so it must not be routed through `protected_from`. Once the keyword exists the existing `grant_keyword` op and `grant_keyword` static carry the whole 'equipped/enchanted creature has shroud' family (~15 further cards already sitting in data/authoring/queue.json) for free.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `hexproof` is the near-miss and it is a different rule. `can_be_targeted` returns True unconditionally when `obj.controller == controller` and only then asks about hexproof, so hexproof stops opponents alone while shroud stops everyone including the controller. Substituting it makes a strictly better creature than the one printed - this 6/6 flying trampler could still be pumped, regenerated or blinked by its own controller, which the printed card forbids. `protection` is the other candidate and is wrong in the opposite direction: docs/card-dsl.md's Protection section argues exactly this asymmetry, and protection is read by four rules (damage, enchant/equip, block, target) rather than one, so a shroud faked as protection would also prevent all damage to the creature and stop it being blocked. It is additionally parameterised over from_types/from_subtypes/from_colors and the loader rejects a `protection` static that names no quality (loader.py: 'protection needs from_types/from_subtypes/from_colors'), so there is no way to spell 'from everything' at all. Nothing else in the vocabulary reaches targeting legality: `lock_abilities` is a permission on activating abilities and is until-end-of-turn, and no `static_filter_keys` entry describes targetability.
